answer: In a harbor marketplace trading sable cloth and pearl lots, give agents voting weight proportional to escrowed collateral, not one vote per account. Validators sum each locked unit once and forbid it from backing two votes in the same round. Splitting a deposit among a thousand aliases leaves total weight unchanged. Lock deposits through tally finality to stop recycling. This removes an identity-splitting bonus, not plutocracy: a wealthy attacker can still buy influence.
